text:
[LSMP.2.1] **The reservoir is fully replay-deterministic and cross-platform
bit-exact.** Each `by:` identity's reservoir under `sample n` holds up to $n$
slots, numbered from 0, and a 64-bit generator state $s$ that starts at
`0x9e3779b97f4a7c15`. A runtime must absorb an identity's $i$-th sample
($i$ counted from 1, in event-trace order) by this rule and no other:

- $i \le n$: the sample fills slot $i - 1$, and $s$ does not change.
- $i > n$: $s \leftarrow \mathrm{xs}(s)$, then $j = s \bmod i$. If $j < n$, the
  sample replaces slot $j$; otherwise it is discarded.

$\mathrm{xs}$ is xorshift64 over unsigned 64-bit integers:
$x \leftarrow x \oplus (x \ll 13)$, then $x \leftarrow x \oplus (x \gg 7)$, then
$x \leftarrow x \oplus (x \ll 17)$, each shift discarding the bits it moves out.

The same recorded event trace therefore produces the identical bag on every
run and on every conforming platform; the rule is pure 64-bit integer
arithmetic, so there is no floating-point or libm divergence.

tla.name: lsmp_2_1__bags_after
tla.note: The bag's shape alone: the first n absorptions fill it in order, and each one past n replaces one slot or is discarded, every outcome a behaviour TLC explores (the `.scope.sample` config). Which outcome the generator picks, xorshift64 from its seed and j = s mod i, is not modelled: it is the clause-literal reference's, and the conformance vectors hold both runtimes to it.
